J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .40,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Shivanna, S/o.B.Basavegowda in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 30.05.2023 at about 03.00 p.m., the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-HY-5188 from Kabbalu towards Sathnoor side and when they reached in front of Charu Party Hall, near Kabbalu Village,
Channapatna - Sathnoor Road, Sathnoor Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District
, the driver of Eicher/Canter bearing Regn.No.KL-07-BB-3999 drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's motor cycle.
Due to which, deceased fell down on the road and wheel of Eicher/Canter ran over deceased's head and he sustained severe injuries and succumbed at the spot.

Thereafter he was shifted to Kanakapura Govt. Hospital, wherein postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to petitioners and later they shifted the body to their native place to perform obsequies and funeral ceremonies for which they have spent .2,00,000/- towards transportation and funeral expenses.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy.
The deceased was doing agriculture and sericulture work and earning a sum of .40,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.

2 3.

In pursuance of notice, though respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel,
but not filed his written statement.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
Respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the driver of Eicher/canter who was riding in zig zig manner, suddenly applied brake and stopped the vehicle without giving any signal/putting parking lights on the middle of the road and thereby caused the accident.

Further this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy of insurance in respect of the Eicher Canter in favour of 1st respondent insured and same was valid for a period from 12.11.2022 to 11.11.2023 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the owner of vehicle willfully entrusted a eicher to a person who did not had a valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that deceased namely Shivanna succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 30.05.2023 at about 03.00 p.m.,
near Kabbalu Village, infront of Charu Party Hall, Channapatna-Sathnoor Road,
Sathnoor Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, while he was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-HY-5188 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Eicher Canter bearing Regn.No.KL-07-BB- 3999 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
6.

In support of the case, the Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased got examined herself as PW.1 and one eye witness got examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.
This Tribunal answers the above issues are as under:

Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,

The eicher lorry caused caused the accident due to which the deceased succumbed to injuries on the spot.
10. The Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased Sri.Shivanna examined as PW.1.
In her chief- examination she deposed that her husband was travelling on motor cycle as a pillion, due to the rash and negligent driving of Eicher/Canter by its driver the accident occurred.
In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of Eicher/Canter, the petitioners produced Ex.P1 First Information lodged by petitioner No.3/son of deceased with police on 30.05.2023.
On the basis of first information lodged by son of deceased, the police registered a case as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
After registration of FIR, police appears to have visited the spot of accident and prepared spot panchanama & sketch as per Ex.P.3 & 4 by describing the place of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicles involved in the accident are mentioned.
Ex.P6 is the Inquest Report.
Ex.P7 is the PM report, wherein deceased Sri.Shivanna is stated to have died due to head injuries sustained in the accident.
The I.O., after thorough investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Eicher/Canter for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC which is marked as Ex.P8.

Ex . P9 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to said notice is marked as Ex.P.10.
11.
The FIR as well as final report is filed against the driver of eicher/canter alleging rashness and negligence against him.
The complaint is lodged against the driver of eicher/canter alleging rash and negligent driving of vehicle by him.
The police have conducted the investigation based on the complaint and filed the final report against the driver of eicher/canter.
The driver of eicher/canter or the owner does not appear to have challenged or questioned filing of FIR or final report.
The final report appears to have been filed by the police after conducting detailed investigation and same does not appear to have been questioned before any appropriate authority.
The final report is filed stating that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of eicher/canter which does not appear to have been challenged.
Nothing contrary to the said documents are placed by the respondents before the court.

4 12.
The respondent No.2 contended that there is negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle also in the cause of accident.
It is contended by respondent No.2 that the deceased fell down in the road due to negligent driving of motorcycle rider and there was negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
In order to substantiate the said aspect, respondent No.2 not furnished satisfactory materials.

Though respondent No.2 contended that the rider of motorcycle was also negligent, the materials placed on record are not sufficient to consider the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
Ex.P1 and P8 does not disclose the aspect of cause of accident by negligence of rider of motorcycle also.
If there was negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle, then said aspect could have been mentioned in FIR or final report.
The aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle could have been brought to light during investigation by police.
But, final report has not been filed against the rider of motorcycle and it has been filed only against driver of eicher/canter.
The manner in which riding of motorcycle by its rider, was negligent is not forthcoming from the materials on record.
The materials on record are not sufficient and satisfactory to consider the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
The respondent not placed sufficient and satisfactory materials in order to substantiate their contention related to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
The oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of eicher/canter in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents placed no satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioners.

So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners indicates that negligent driving of driver of eicher/canter is the cause for the accident in which Shivanna succumbed due to injuries caused.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioner coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher/Canter bearing Regn.No.KL-07-BB-3999 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
The petitioners succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher/Canter bearing registration Regn.No.KL-07-BB-3999 by its driver.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., in order to assess the compensation.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Sri.Shivanna, S/o B.Basavegowda is shown as 55 years.

In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners furnished Ex.P.12,
Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1958.
As per the said document, the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 65 years.
The accident occurred on 30.05.2023 and date of birth of deceased in 01.01.1958.
So, age of deceased was 65 years as on the date of accident.
The materials on record discloses the age of deceased to be 65 years as on the date of accident and as such, same is taken into consideration.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable in present Kamalamma vs Rajesha.N on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185878133/
5 case is '07'.

sentences.text: (ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Shivanna was doing an Agriculture and Sericulture work and earning a sum of .40,000/- per month.
In order to substantiate the said aspect, the petitioners furnished the pass book issued by Sericulture department, four receipts and RTC extract which are marked as Ex.P.13 to P.15.
Ex . P.13
is issued in the name of deceased Shivanna and the name of deceased Shivanna is entered in Ex.P.15, which pertains to Sy.No.81/2 of Deveerahalli village.
The said documents substantiate the contention of petitioners that deceased Shivanna was doing sericulture and agriculture.
Though the said documents disclose the occupation of deceased Shivanna, they will not substantiate the contention regarding the income of Shivanna.

The said documents are not sufficient to consider that deceased Shivanna was having income of .40,000/-
per month.
Ex . P.14, receipts, do not assist in ascertaining the actual and specific monthly income of deceased Shivanna.
The said document cannot be considered sufficient to consider the fixed income as .40,000/- per month.
Ex . P.14

discloses the date as November 2022 and no previous receipts are furnished by petitioners in order to ascertain that the income mentioned in the said document is the fixed monthly income of deceased Shivanna.
Ex. P.13 to P.15 are not sufficient to consider that deceased Shivanna was earning .40,000/- per month.
Ex.P.13 to P.15 are not sufficient to substantiate the contention of petitioners that deceased Shivanna was having monthly income of .40,000/-.
Ex.P.15 is also not of much assistance in ascertaining the actual income derived from the said property.
Though deceased Shivanna appears to have property, no materials are being placed to show ascertained income derived from the said property.
As no satisfactory materials are placed by petitioner related to income of deceased, as per their contention, the notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is to be taken into consideration.
On perusal of the materials on record, the notional income is considered as .16,000/- per month.
At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 65 years.
So, In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others Hon'be Supreme Court, the petitioners are not entitled for future prospects.

sentences.text: Admittedly deceased Sri.Shivanna is married and died leaving behind wife and children.
In order to prove the relationship with deceased, the petitioners furnished notarized copies of Aadhaar Cards, which are marked at Ex.P12.
As per the recitals of said document, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased Shivanna.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to doubt or disprove the genuineness or authenticity of said documents.
The respondents not furnished any materials in order to dispute the relationship of petitioners with deceased Shivanna.

In 2020 ACJ 759 between National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Birender and others, the Hon'ble Apex Court held at para-15 that: -
"15.

entities.text: 2020 ACJ 759 between National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Birender and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to Kamalamma vs Rajesha.N on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185878133/
6 consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
Petitioners No.1 to 3 are wife and children of deceased respectively.
On perusal of the cause title of the petition, petitioner No.2 appears to be married.
Though petitioner No.2 is married, she is considered to be legal representative of deceased Shivanna and she is entitled to claim compensation.

In view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the above reported judgment,
petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered as legal representatives of deceased Shivanna and entitled to claim compensation.
The materials on record disclose that petitioner No.2 is married which aspect is admitted by PW.1 during the cross examination.
The petitioners not placed sufficient and satisfactory materials to consider that petitioner No.2 is dependent on the income of deceased Shivanna.
No materials are placed to show that petitioner No.2 is dependent on deceased Shivanna.
As such, though petitioner No.2 is considered as legal representative of deceased Shivanna, she cannot be considered to be a dependent.
The petitioners contended that they are dependent on the income of deceased Shivanna.
As discussed above, no materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that petitioner No.2 is dependent on the income of deceased Shivanna.
Petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1, wherein she stated that they are dependent on the income of Shivanna.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent No.2 and in the cross examination, nothing to dispute or doubt the dependancy of petitioner No.1 and 3 could be elicited in the cross examination.
In the cross examination, PW.1 stated that petitioner No.3 is not doing any work and she is also not able to do any agricultural work.
On consideration of said aspect and the materials on record, petitioner No.1 and 3 are considered to be dependents of deceased Shivanna.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt. Saral Verma case where number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.
As discussed above, the notional income of deceased Shivanna is taken for consideration which is .16,000/-.

Thus petitioners are entitled to compensation of .8,96,028/- towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:
 Calculation Total (In R.)
 1/3rd of .16,000/- .10,667/-
 (deduction) (5,333/-)
.10,667/- multiply by 12 .1,28,004/- annual income .1,28,004/- multiply by .8,96,028/- 07 (Multiplier) (B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;
In the present case, the date of accident is 30.05.2023.

So, in view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case, the petitioners are entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which has to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in a span of three years.
So the petitioner No.1 to 3 being the wife and children of deceased are entitled for .48,400/- (each) towards loss of Spousal Consortium and Parental Consortium Petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children
are entitled for .18,150/- towards loss of estate and .18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

15. Thus, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation as follows:

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of .10,77,528/-.
16.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
17. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher/Canter bearing Regn.No.KL-07-BB- 3999 by its driver.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .10,77,528/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Seventy Seven Thousand Five Hundred and Twenty Eight only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 to 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 3, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 30.05.2023 at about 03-00 p.m., near Kabbalu Village, infront of Charu Party Hall, Channapatna - Sathnoor Road, Sathnoor Hobali, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramangara District, due to the rash and negligent driving of Eicher/Canter bearing Regn.No.KL-07-BB- 3999 by its driver, while he was traveling on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-HY-5188 as a pillion rider.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petitioners succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher/Canter bearing registration Regn.No.KL-07-BB-3999 by its driver.
The Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., in order to assess the compensation.
The said document cannot be considered sufficient to consider the fixed income as .40,000/- per month.
As no satisfactory materials are placed by petitioner related to income of deceased, as per their contention, the notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is to be taken into consideration.
On perusal of the materials on record, the notional income is considered as .16,000/- per month.
At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 65 years.
So, In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others Hon'be Supreme Court, the petitioners are not entitled for future prospects.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to doubt or disprove the genuineness or authenticity of said documents.
The respondents not furnished any materials in order to dispute the relationship of petitioners with deceased Shivanna.
On perusal of the cause title of the petition, petitioner No.2 appears to be married.
Though petitioner No.2 is married, she is considered to be legal representative of deceased Shivanna and she is entitled to claim compensation.
The materials on record disclose that petitioner No.2 is married which aspect is admitted by PW.1 during the cross examination.
The petitioners not placed sufficient and satisfactory materials to consider that petitioner No.2 is dependent on the income of deceased Shivanna.
No materials are placed to show that petitioner No.2 is dependent on deceased Shivanna.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 60%, petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children of deceased are entitled for 20% each of the compensation amount.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 to 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 3, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
